newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-WILKINS, MAXWELL LEAD UNDERMANNED SPURS PAST TIRED LAKERS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-WILKINS, MAXWELL LEAD UNDERMANNED SPURS PAST TIRED LAKERS.

text.p: Dominique Wilkins scored a season-high 28 points and Vernon Maxwell added 22 as the undermanned San Antonio Spurs surprised the fatigued Los Angeles Lakers 95-83 on Wednesday.

"It was David versus Goliath tonight," said Spurs point guard Avery Johnson, who had 16 points and 10 assists. "We were staring 1-6 in the face. However, David won tonight. Goliath was on the floor unconscious."

The loss could prove to be a costly one for Los Angeles (5-3). Lakers forward Cedric Ceballos was carried off the floor on a stretcher with 3:48 remaining after suffering a partial tear of his right patella tendon.
Ceballos will be examined Thursday in Los Angeles.
Wilkins also grabbed 11 rebounds for San Antonio, which snapped a three-game losing streak despite playing without three starters.
Centre David Robinson has missed every game this season with back problems, and will be out at least another week. Forward Charles Smith and guard Vinny Del Negro sat out with knee injuries.

Shaquille O'Neal had 30 points and 10 rebounds and Eddie Jones added 22 points for the Lakers, who were coming off Tuesday's double-overtime win against Houston. Los Angeles has lost seven straight regular-season games in San Antonio and has never won in the AlamoDome.

"We were dragging and tired and a step slow," said Lakers guard Byron Scott. "There were no excuses for the loss. We weren't as mentally prepared as we should have been. San Antonio was ready, we weren't."
"Obviously we need to do a better job on back-to-back games, because we have eight more this season," said Los Angeles coach Del Harris.
In Toronto, rookie Marcus Camby scored 23 points as the Raptors cruised to a 110-98 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers, who had their three-game winning streak snapped.
Walt Williams scored 22 points and Damon Stoudamire added 21 points and 12 assists for the Raptors, who ended a three-game losing streak against the 76ers.
The game featured this year's top two draft picks and last year's Rookie of the Year.
Camby, the second overall pick in the NBA draft, added five blocks to his 23 points. Top pick Allen Iverson scored 24 points for the Sixers.
Iverson was 8-of-18 from the field and committed five turnovers. But he forced Stoudamire, the 1996 Rookie of the Year, into 8-of-28 shooting and seven turnovers.
"I think he's the quickest player I've seen one-on-one," Camby said of Iverson.
"Marcus Camby played really well tonight," Iverson said. "They got the victory, so that speaks for itself."

In Chicago, Michael Jordan scored 28 points and Toni Kukoc added 26 as the Bulls extended the best start in franchise history and remained the league's only unbeaten team with a 103-71 rout of the Miami Heat.
The Bulls have won their first eight games and are ahead of last-season's pace, when they won a record 72 games.
Alonzo Mourning led Miami with 20 points. Both Heat losses in seven games this season have come to Chicago.

In Detroit, Grant Hill scored 27 points, including a pair of free throws with 5.5 seconds left in overtime, to lead the Pistons to a 95-94 victory over the Denver Nuggets for their sixth win in seven games.
Detroit is off to its best start since winning the first eight games of the 1988-89 season, when they won their first NBA championship.
At Utah, Karl Malone scored 22 points in three quarters and Bryon Russell added 15 as the Jazz breezed past the Sacramento Kings for the 11th straight time, 105-74.
Second-year centre Greg Ostertag had his best NBA game with 14 points and 13 rebounds and John Stockton added 13 points and 10 assists for the Jazz.
The Kings trailed by as many as 39 points and lost for the fourth time in five games.
At New Jersey, Chris Webber scored 26 points as the Washington Bullets snapped a three-game losing streak with a 106-91 victory over the winless Nets.
Juwan Howard added 22 points for the Bullets.
Rookie Kerry Kittles, making his first start, scored 12 of his 21 points in the final quarter for the Nets (0-4).

In Cleveland, Danny Ferry scored four of his 15 points in a decisive fourth-quarter 11-0 run and Chris Mills added a key three-pointer late in the game as the Cavaliers defeated the Portland Trail Blazers 81-70.
The Cavaliers' defence held Portland to its regular-season record low point total.
In Boston, Dana Barros came off the bench to score 18 points and David Wesley added 16 as the Celtics defeated the Atlanta Hawks for the first time in seven attempts with a 103-85 rout.
